I have been growing stevia on this land for several years now. It is a good cash crop — the buyers come and take the dried leaves, and the price is stable enough. My plot is small, 1.1 mu, so I manage it mostly myself and with help from family when they are not working in town.

Stevia needs transplanting from seedlings in late April after the last frost. I buy improved seedlings from the local agricultural supply station — I tried traditional cuttings years ago but the improved variety gives me better leaf yield and the buyers prefer it. My well gives me reliable water, which matters because Quzhou gets dry in summer. I plan to irrigate about 10 times through the season, more frequently in July and August when it is hottest.

I will apply base fertilizer before transplanting — some compound fertilizer with nitrogen and phosphorus — then top-dress after each cut. Stevia gives me two, maybe three cuts per season: first in July, second in September. After each cut I add some urea to push regrowth. I do rotary tillage before planting to loosen the soil, as I always do.

Aphids and whiteflies can damage the leaves, which lowers quality at sale. I will spray about four times — early prevention is better than waiting. I do not want chemical residue either, so I am careful about timing before harvest.

With 1.1 mu all in stevia and good irrigation, I expect around 300 kg of dried leaf this year.
